doc.name: A — pet accessories catalogue, botanical set, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: waxed-canvas dog collar
Category: pet accessories
Shot programme: botanical set
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this pet accessories product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-context lifestyle in a botanical set treatment.

SUBJECT. A waxed-canvas dog collar. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Product in its real use environment with lived-in supporting props. Shoot on a 180mm long macro at f/1.8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard low sun raking across the surface with long cast shadows. Stage the product on or against oiled walnut, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
